headline: Dry season runs November to April
detail: February to April are the driest months; March averages about 10 rainy days. Sandbars, island hopping and open-boat crossings are all at their best in this window.

headline: June to November is typhoon season
detail: The peak is September and October. Sea legs are the first thing to go and no amount of planning books around a suspended crossing.

headline: Rough seas cancel crossings the same day
detail: Sailings stop automatically when the Philippine Coast Guard declares a no-sail policy. Single habagat and typhoon events in 2026 suspended Masbate City-Lagundi, Bulan-San Jacinto, Bulan-San Fernando, San Pascual, Aroroy and Pasacao at once. Treat every sea leg as cancellable on the morning and keep a spare day.

headline: Carry the whole trip in cash
detail: Withdraw before you leave the mainland. There is no ATM in San Pascual and cards are not accepted on any island circuit. Bring small notes - boatmen and habal-habal drivers rarely carry change.

headline: RoRo boarding wants a government ID and an early arrival
detail: Operators ask for a valid government-issued ID at the gate and want passengers aboard up to two hours before the scheduled departure.

headline: Rodeo Masbateno fills the city in the second week of April
detail: The 30th edition ran 9-13 April 2026. Rooms in Masbate City go early that week and the city itself is the attraction.

headline: Most Burias trips start in Quezon or Camarines Sur, not in Masbate
detail: San Andres in Quezon and Pasacao in Camarines Sur are two to three hours out. Routing from Masbate City means roughly six hours at sea to Claveria first, on a crossing with no published fare.

headline: Book the boat at the San Pascual tourism office by the port
detail: Island hopping is arranged at the municipal tourism office beside San Pascual port, at a fixed posted rate. There is no tourism desk on any of the islands.

headline: Island entrance fees are collected on arrival on top of the boat
detail: Sombrero PHP 20 and Tinalisayan PHP 10 per person. Camping runs PHP 150-300 and a cottage PHP 300-400.

headline: Nothing is sold on the islets
detail: Animasola has no eatery, toilet, shower or cottage. Carry water, food, a dry bag and a trash bag, and take the rubbish back out with you.

headline: Power on the islets cuts around midnight
detail: Bring a power bank or spare batteries if you are camping.

headline: Mobile data is weak to absent on the islets
detail: Reports conflict - some visitors get a usable signal across Burias, others none at all on the outer islands. Assume no connectivity once you leave San Pascual.

headline: The Tinalisayan sandbar is a low-tide feature
detail: The bar surfaces through the day and is under water at high tide. Time the boat around the tide, not the clock.

headline: Ticao island hopping leaves from Monreal port
detail: Halea, Catandayagan, Burubangkaso, Mababoy and Lapus-Lapus are one hired boat out of Monreal, not separate trips.

headline: The Monreal boat hire steps up by boat size
detail: About PHP 2,500 for up to 5, up to about PHP 8,000 for 15 and over, plus a PHP 500 guide fee. Per-person cost jumps at each boat size rather than falling smoothly with party size.

headline: PHP 25 environmental fee plus a docking fee at Halea
detail: Collected by Monreal Tourism on arrival, on top of the boat hire and the guide fee.

headline: Mantas are a December-to-May proposition
detail: Sightings are most reliable December to May and peak March to June, when the monsoon current drives the plankton bloom. Whale sharks run November to June and are densest in February and May.

headline: Manta Bowl is an advanced dive, not a snorkelling stop
detail: Tidal currents regularly exceed 3 knots and entries are negative-entry drift dives. Advanced Open Water certification and a booking through one of the San Jacinto dive camps are the practical minimum.

headline: Currents run strong inside the Lapus-Lapus lagoon
detail: The lagoon is sheltered from the monsoon swell but not from the current. Do not read the calm surface as safe swimming.

headline: Last fastcraft off Ticao is 15:00 from Lagundi
detail: Masbate City departs 10:00, 14:00 and 16:00; Lagundi departs 07:00, 11:00 and 15:00. Forty minutes each way.

headline: The last pumpboat off Ticao goes in the early afternoon
detail: Last departure from Masbate City Fish Port around 13:00 and from Lagundi around 14:00, three to four sailings a day. This is a 2018 figure and the only one published - confirm at the fish port.

headline: The Bulan crossing now runs three times a day, not five
detail: A May 2026 listing has Bulan departing 08:30, 12:30 and 15:30 and San Jacinto 05:30, 10:00 and 13:00, operated by Barrun Sealines with MV Marilou. One hour by fastcraft, about 1.5 hours by RoRo. The feed still carries the 2017 five-sailing pattern.

headline: The Buntod sandbar is a low-tide feature
detail: At high water there is barely a bar to stand on. Check the tide before you pay for the boat, not after.

headline: Register at the ranger station on arrival
detail: Boats leave from Rendezvous Beach Resort and the ranger station on the sandbar handles registration. The City Tourism Office at Masbate City Hall will arrange the visit if you would rather not turn up cold.

headline: PHP 20 entrance and a PHP 100 boat docking fee on top of the hire
detail: A day cottage is about PHP 300, an umbrella with two chairs PHP 100, an overnight cottage about PHP 500.

headline: Walk Pawa between 15:00 and 18:00
detail: Morning to noon is high tide. The late-afternoon low is when the boardwalk is worth the trip, and it is also the cooler end of the day.

headline: Pawa is free and needs no booking
detail: The tricycle is the only cost. Get off at the NE Delos Santos Elementary School arch, then it is about 20 minutes on foot through the village to the far end of the 1.3 km boardwalk.

headline: There is no same-day public boat back from Bugui Point
detail: The public boat leaves Aroroy Port at 11:00, PHP 50, about an hour - and the return is 06:00 the next morning. A day trip means chartering: about PHP 800 round trip for up to four, quoted as high as PHP 1,500.

headline: Last van to Balud leaves Masbate City about 16:00
detail: Around PHP 175 and two hours by UV Express. Miss it and Palani becomes an overnight.

headline: Take a guide into Bat-ongan
detail: Entrance is PHP 10-20 and a guide PHP 150-250. Guides are residents at the foot of the hill and every account says a first-timer should not go in without one.

headline: PHP 30 entrance including the environmental fee
detail: Summit cottages rent from about PHP 200 a night. The view takes in Masbate City and the Buntod sandbar, and it is a sunset and stargazing spot as much as a hike.

headline: No scheduled boat runs to Nagarao
detail: Charter a motorised bangka at Barangay Pasiagon in Placer. Nothing is published about the rate, so agree it before you board.

headline: La Manok is easier to reach from Cebu than from Masbate
detail: 35-45 minutes by boat from Carnaza Island in Cebu against 50-60 minutes from the Masbate side. The island is uninhabited with no facilities, and the sandbar joining its two halves goes under at high tide.
